title: Wild that my second most expensive show of the year was a LOTTERY win...
transcript: I saw over 200 shows this year and this is how much I spent just ripping off the Band Aid. The total that I spent this year is four thousand seven hundred eighty one dollars and twenty five cents, which unfortunately is a 67% increase from last year. I do wanna point out that this is just the cost of the tickets themselves and does not factor in things like travel or accommodation. So in reality this number is probably much higher when you consider things like flights to London, trains from London and Edinburgh, my accommodation in Scotland and London, as well as my various trips regionally to D C. And Boston. However, breaking that down, that is about $398 per month, or $24 a ticket. And since I get a lot of comps, if you remove the tickets that I got for free, then it's $36 per ticket, which I still think is pretty good in terms of what I paid. Over half of my tickets were less than $25, with 68 of them being comps, meaning either I got invited or my friend was invited and took me as their plus one. And 49 of them I paid for but were less than $25. 68 tickets were between $25 and $50, 16 tickets were between $50 and $100. And then finally there was only one ticket that was over $100. We'll get to that later. Looking at cost per month, I was actually really surprised that August Was not my most expensive month. If you remember from my previous video, I saw the most theatre in August with 50 shows, thanks largely to the Edinburgh Fringe, where I saw 37 shows in five days. However, since I was a credited press for fringe, I saw a lot of those for free, and the ones that I did pay for were honestly super inexpensive. So I ended up with a total of $699 for that month, which is not quite as high as April where I spent $749 for the month. And my cheapest month was December where I spent a very reasonable $210. Which brings me to my biggest splurges. My fifth most expensive ticket was the Patty Lapone Life in notes concert at Carnegie Hall, which I paid ninety one dollars and fifty cents for. My fourth most expensive ticket was Starlight Express in London, which I paid ninety six dollars and eighty cents for. My third most expensive ticket was 25th Annual Putnam County Spelling Bee at the Kennedy Center, which I paid ninety seven dollars and fifty cents for. My second most expensive ticket was Sleep No More, which I paid $99 for thanks to a lottery win. And finally, my most expensive ticket was the Follies concert, also at Carnegie Hall, which I paid $108 for.
